title: scan_history.team_id is never written by any scan path, so team scan sharing is dead end to end while shipping a full UI for it
description: PATCH /api/v3/history/[id] destructures teamId at :267, authorizes it at :313-326 and writes it at :349-352. That is the only write path to scan_history.team_id (instrumentation.ts:928) in the entire codebase. Every INSERT INTO scan_history omits the column: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:368, scan/crawl/route.ts:440, scan/bulk/route.ts:278, scan/authenticated/route.ts:469, scan/github/route.ts:252, lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts:280, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:633. No UI ever sends teamId: the only PATCH bodies sent are {notes} (app/history/page.tsx:394) and {isPublic} (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:339); a repo-wide grep for 'share to team' / 'share with team' across .tsx returns zero. The sibling columns webhooks.team_id (instrumentation.ts:934) and scheduled_scans.team_id (:937) have the same shape: PATCH accepts teamId (webhooks/[id]/route.ts:201, schedules/route.ts:308) and no UI sends it.
impact: GET /api/v3/teams/member-scans queries WHERE user_id = $1 AND team_id = $2 (app/api/v3/teams/member-scans/route.ts:53-60) and can only ever return an empty array, yet the product ships a complete viewer for it with pagination (app/teams/page.tsx:469, components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx). Every getTeamResourceAccess team branch across history, share and report is unreachable. The feature is documented and sold at app/docs/teams/page.tsx:374-380. A paying team customer sees an empty panel with no explanation.
recommendation: Add a 'Share with team' control to components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx beside the existing 'Make private' item at :590, populated from getAssignableTeamIds with a 'Personal (private)' null option, plus a team column and filter on History. Add the same selector to the webhook and schedule rows on Profile > Developer. Alternatively decide the feature is not wanted and remove the columns, the read paths and the docs section.

title: Every API code sample and the OpenAPI `servers` URL hardcode https://vulnradar.dev on any build without NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, including the published Docker image
description: lib/config/constants.ts:191 resolves `APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL`, and lib/config/config-values.ts:141 sets CONFIG_APP_URL to "https://vulnradar.dev". NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined by Next at build time, and .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49-51 runs `docker build -t $IMAGE:${VERSION} -t $IMAGE:latest .` with no `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, even though Dockerfile:16/32 declares the ARG. So the published GHCR image bakes vulnradar.dev into APP_URL. app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts:11 calls `buildOpenApiSpec(APP_URL)`, which lands in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:25 as `servers: [{ url: "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3" }]` (its own docstring at :12-13 claims "baseUrl is the deployment's origin so a self-hosted instance advertises its own server"). app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 reads `spec.servers[0].url` as its baseUrl and :298/:316 fetch that absolute URL. Every curl/JS sample on app/docs/api/page.tsx:935-984, the rate-limits backoff samples (app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:379/413), and the reports curl samples (app/docs/reports/page.tsx:296/449) interpolate the same APP_URL.
impact: On a self-hosted instance run from the official image, every documented curl command targets the public SaaS instead of the operator's own deployment, and the playground's "Send request" button issues a cross-origin request to vulnradar.dev that fails CORS with the opaque message "Request failed (network, CORS, or an invalid URL)". The playground's own setup text ("the key ... is sent only to https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3") then tells the operator their key goes to someone else's server.
recommendation: Pass `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49, or (better, since the image is shared) make app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts call resolveAppUrl(request) from lib/config/runtime-config.ts instead of the compiled APP_URL, and have app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 fall back to `window.location.origin + "/api/v3"` when the spec's server host does not match the current origin.

title: The `main` branch has no branch protection and no ruleset, so not one CI job is a required check and every ci.yml comment claiming a step blocks merges is false
description: I queried the public GitHub API for this repository. `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/branches/main` returns `protected: false` with `protection.required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"` and empty `contexts` and `checks` arrays; `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/rules/branches/main` returns an empty array, so no repository ruleset applies either. ci.yml runs five jobs on `pull_request: branches: [main]` (lint, typecheck, test, extension, build) and its comments assert they gate merges: line 43 "format drift should block merges", lines 65-66 "removed `continue-on-error: true`. Typecheck must block merges", line 70 "block merges on high/critical CVEs in runtime deps". None of these are required checks, so a red CI run is advisory only and the merge button stays green. The same absence means .github/CODEOWNERS is decorative: CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers but only enforces review when "Require review from Code Owners" is set in branch protection, and it is not. Direct pushes to main are also unrestricted.
impact: The entire CI investment (SHA-pinned actions, a Prettier gate, a hard typecheck, an `npm audit` gate on 71 runtime dependencies, an extension build, a Next.js build) enforces nothing. Broken TypeScript, a failing test suite, or a high-severity CVE in a production dependency can be merged or pushed straight to main with a single click, and the next `v*` tag turns that into a published image and a GitHub release. It also means the two-person review flow the CODEOWNERS file describes is not actually required for lib/auth, lib/billing, or .github.
recommendation: Add a ruleset (or classic branch protection) on `main` that requires the Lint, Typecheck, Test, Extension, and Build check names, requires at least one approving review, requires review from code owners, and blocks force pushes and direct pushes. Commit the ruleset JSON under .github/ so the configuration is reviewable in-repo rather than living only in the web UI.

title: Dependabot auto-merge calls `gh pr merge --auto` into an unprotected main, so with zero required checks a dependency bump merges the instant it opens, before CI has run
description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:32 runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash "$PR_URL"` for any dependabot PR whose `update-type` is `version-update:semver-patch` (line 30) and which lacks the `dependabot-merge-ignore` label. The workflow header at line 3 states the guarantee: "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes." `--auto` does not wait for CI; it waits for the PR to become mergeable under the branch's protection rules. Per ci-02, `main` has `protected: false`, `required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`, empty `contexts`, and no ruleset, so a dependabot PR is mergeable at the moment it opens and auto-merge fires immediately, with lint, typecheck, test and build still queued or running. The workflow grants itself `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` at lines 11-13. Separately, ci.yml's `npm ci` steps (lines 37, 62, 101, 138, 193) run with no `--ignore-scripts` and .npmrc contains only `audit-level=high`, `fund=false`, `update-notifier=false`, so package lifecycle scripts execute in CI. (If the repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting happens to be off, `gh pr merge --auto` errors instead and the entire workflow is dead on every dependabot PR; that is the alternative reading and is also a finding.)
impact: A compromised patch release of any of the 71 runtime dependencies is merged to main with no human review and without a single CI job having passed, and its install scripts then run in every subsequent CI job. The next `v*` tag builds that main into the published GHCR image and the signed release tarball, so the compromise propagates to every self-hosted install through the in-app updater. The `npm audit --audit-level=high` gate at ci.yml:71 only catches advisories that already exist, which by definition a fresh malicious release does not have. The stated safety property ("after CI passes") is not enforced anywhere in the repository.
recommendation: Fix ci-02 first: `--auto` is only meaningful once required status checks exist. Then either require Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build as checks on main, or replace `--auto` with an explicit gate in this workflow (a `needs:` on a job that re-runs the suite, or `gh pr checks --watch` before merging). Also restrict auto-merge to devDependencies, or add a cooldown so a package released in the last N days is never auto-merged.

title: Self-hosting is the differentiator that beats six of the eight commercial peers, it is asserted in six separate marketing surfaces, and AUDIT-014#host-01 proves it does not currently work
category: competitive positioning: list (b), the load-bearing advantage
description: Of the eight commercial DAST vendors researched (Detectify, Intruder, Probely/Snyk, Pentest-Tools.com, Acunetix/Invicti, Burp Suite DAST, Snyk, Astra), only Burp Suite DAST and Acunetix/Invicti offer real self-hosting; the other six are SaaS with at most an internal-scanning agent (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Deployment" section). GPL-3.0 plus a working self-host is therefore the single structural advantage that no amount of engineering by a small team could otherwise buy. The product asserts it in six places: components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:39 ("Self-hosting is one Dockerfile and a Postgres connection string"), app/landing/page.tsx:82 (FAQ: "Yes. The whole thing is GPL-3.0 and runs on your own infrastructure"), app/landing/page.tsx:57 (the definitional FAQ answer), components/landing/landing-use-cases.tsx:21 ("a self-host path if the SaaS is a non-starter"), lib/seo/alternatives.ts:46 (the shared VR.hosting string reused on all five /alternatives pages), and lib/seo/alternatives.ts:103, :250, :317 (per-competitor FAQ answers repeating it). AUDIT-014#host-01 (critical) found that on an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and AUDIT-014#host-02 found the Dockerfile runtime stage never copies scripts/, so db:create and db:migrate are unrunnable inside the published image. Merged from mkt-03, which filed the same fact from the marketing surface. Its point stands and is folded in here: the recommendation is to keep the self-hosting copy rather than weaken it, because the marketing surface is itself the argument for prioritising the host-01 and host-02 fixes. If they cannot be fixed quickly, the copy has to change instead, since it is currently false on the landing page and in the README.
impact: Every competitive claim on the site rests on a capability that a new self-hoster cannot currently exercise. A developer who reaches /alternatives/detectify, reads "self-host it yourself with no plan limits", clones the repo and fails at first boot does not file a bug: they conclude the open-source claim is decorative and leave. This is the one advantage the eight commercial peers structurally cannot copy, and it is the one that does not work.
recommendation: Treat AUDIT-014#host-01 and #host-02 as competitive-blocking, not just deploy bugs: fix them before any further marketing or SEO work in section 19. Then add a CI job that runs the documented self-host path end to end (fresh Postgres container, docker compose up, assert /api/v3/health returns healthy) so the claim cannot silently rot again. Only once that job is green, promote self-hosting from a paragraph in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx to a named comparison row in lib/seo/alternatives.ts's shared VR object, phrased against the verified fact: "Self-host it. Six of the eight commercial web scanners cannot be run on your own infrastructure at any price."

title: Four marketing surfaces claim scans finish in under 3 seconds while the shipped scan path still awaits a 15s subdomain discovery, so the visitor watches the claim fail on the first scan
description: The under-3-seconds claim is published in five places: app/landing/page.tsx:31 (the page meta description, "get a security report in under 3 seconds"), app/landing/page.tsx:77 (the FAQ answer "Under 3 seconds for a standard scan", which is also emitted as FAQPage structured data via FaqStructuredData at :110), components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:61 (the stat strip entry ["<3s", "per scan"]), components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:46 ("Most scans are done in under three seconds"), and README.md:8. components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx:23 also ships a sample response with "duration": 2841. AUDIT-011#scan-01 established the engine does not meet that on the signed-in path, and the cause is still present: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-795 still awaits autoSubdomainsPromise, capped at 15000ms by lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts, and components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 still starts the client stopwatch that AUDIT-011#scan-05 measured at 15 to 20 seconds. Verified at those exact lines in the current tree. The only surface where the claim holds is the demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts skips subdomain discovery entirely, which means the visitor sees 3 seconds in the demo and 17 seconds on their first real scan.
impact: The product's headline differentiator is contradicted by the product roughly thirty seconds after the visitor reads it, on the first scan they run as a signed-up user. A specific number that turns out to be wrong by 5x is worse than no number, because it teaches the reader that the rest of the page's very specific claims (stable IDs, deterministic severities, real evidence) may be equally decorative. The FAQ answer is also syndicated as FAQPage structured data, so the false number is what an answer engine quotes.
recommendation: Fix the engine, do not soften the copy: AUDIT-011#scan-01 specifies a roughly 10-line change at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-802 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698 that makes every one of these five claims true again. If that will not ship this cycle, remove the number rather than publish a false one. Interim copy: app/landing/page.tsx:31 becomes "Paste a URL and get ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} deterministic checks back across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets. Same URL, same finding IDs, every run. No agent to install." app/landing/page.tsx:75-78 FAQ becomes question "How long does a scan take?" answer "Checks run in parallel rather than in sequence, and the report shows the exact duration for your target. Slow DNS or a long certificate chain is what moves the number." components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:58-63 drops the speed stat and becomes [[checkCount, "checks"], [categoryCount, "categories"], ["0", "models in the detection path"], ["GPL-3.0", "licensed"]], which keeps the mono tabular-nums idiom and swaps the one number the product cannot back for the one differentiator it can. components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:45-49 becomes "Everything runs in parallel, so the wall clock is the slowest module, not the sum of them. The report tells you exactly how long yours took."

title: /admin is 20 tabs grouped by data model inside one 1,683-line client component, so the three tasks an operator actually performs each cross three to seven of them
description:
The whole admin surface is one client component. `VALID_TABS` (app/admin/page.tsx:112-133) declares 20 destinations, `ActiveTab` (:152-172) repeats the same 20 as a union, and `NAV_GROUPS_RAW` (:689-835) sorts them into 6 groups: User Management (users, teams, admins), Security (access-rules, blocked-data, security-alerts, audit), Communications (broadcast, notifications, ai-chats, support-tickets), Content (content), Billing (billing-overview), System (settings, updater, backup, queue-status, error-logs, email-logs, engine-feedback). Every group name is a data-model noun, not a job. The System group alone holds 7 unrelated destinations that share nothing except not fitting elsewhere: an update installer, a backup runner, a scanner-queue gauge, two log viewers, a settings editor and a detection-tuning tool. Content is a group of one. Billing is a group of one. The panel body is 20 sibling `{activeTab === X && <Manager/>}` lines (:1182-1674) with no route split, and AUDIT-012#fe-11 already measured the cost: 22 eagerly imported managers in one 1,333 KB route. The growth is visible in the leftovers: a 31-entry toast-label map inlined at :530-562, a stale 5-tab table still exported from components/admin/config.ts:7-17 (AUDIT-013#dead-01), and an empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk directory (AUDIT-011#bulk-06).

Measured click cost of the three most common operator tasks today.

A) Resolve a support ticket that needs the requester's account state. 1 click Support in the nav, 2 click the ticket, 3 select and copy the requester email (support-inbox.tsx:253 renders `owner_email` as plain text, no link), 4 click Users in the nav (handleTabChange at :869-876 calls setSelectedUser(null) and rewrites the URL, so the open ticket is gone), 5 click the search box and paste, wait the 300 ms debounce at :599, 6 click the user row, 7 click Support again, 8 click the ticket again to re-read it. Seven clicks plus a copy-paste, and the ticket view is rebuilt from scratch twice.

B) The morning check, is anything wrong right now. The panel lands on `activeTab = "users"` (:203). Scanner Queue is 1 click, Error Logs 2, Security Alerts 3, Backups 4, Email Logs 5, Support 6. Six clicks, six panels that each refetch on mount with their own poll interval, and the operator does the staleness arithmetic on the backup date themselves. Only one of the 20 nav items carries any status indicator at all (the updater dot, :1087-1092).

C) Apply a support fix to one user, for example reset a daily scan limit. Type in the search box, 1 click the row, then scroll past Overview, Account Management, Staff Role and Badges and Admin Notes to reach Support Actions (user-detail-panel.tsx:1872), 2 click the right card out of 21 laid out in a `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (:1894), 3 confirm. Three clicks, but the cost is scanning 21 near-identical cards, not the clicks.
impact: An operator cannot form a mental model of the panel from its navigation, because the navigation describes the database rather than the work. Cross-referencing is the normal case in support and the panel makes it the expensive case: task A costs seven clicks and destroys the operator's place twice. Task B, the one that protects the service, costs six clicks and is therefore skipped, which is how the failures AUDIT-012#obs-02 and AUDIT-012#obs-03 found stay invisible. New destinations get appended to whichever group is least wrong, so the drift compounds.
recommendation:
Regroup by operator job and split the route. Seven sections, 17 destinations, one home.

1. Operations (new default landing, replaces users as the initial tab at app/admin/page.tsx:203). Home view described in qols-02. Children: Scanner Queue, Error Logs, Email Logs, Backups, Updater. This merges the five System-group destinations that are all one question, is the machine healthy.
2. People. Users (search-first, see below), Teams, Staff and Invites (today's Active Staff plus the invite modal from staff-list.tsx).
3. Support. Tickets, AI Chats. Moves ai-chats out of Communications: reading a user's conversation is support and moderation work, not messaging.
4. Trust and Safety. Security Alerts, Access Rules, Blocked Data, Hosts and Shares (today's single-item Content group). Merges four scattered destinations into the one job, deciding what a user or an IP is allowed to do.
5. Billing. Billing Overview, plus a gifted-subscriptions list (today gifts are only visible per-user through user-detail-panel.tsx:2251).
6. Messaging. Broadcast, Notifications. Both are tell users something; today they sit in Communications next to two support tools.
7. Configuration. Settings, Engine Feedback, Audit Log.

Searchable rather than browsable: Users, Audit Log, Error Logs, Email Logs, AI Chats are all logs you query. Users should open on a search field with recent-activity results underneath, not a paginated directory of every account.

Mechanics: give each destination its own route segment under app/admin/(section)/, which deletes the 20-branch conditional at :1182-1674 and fixes AUDIT-012#fe-11 for free. Move the tab table out of app/admin/page.tsx into a single exported ADMIN_SECTIONS in components/admin/config.ts (replacing the stale ADMIN_TABS at config.ts:7-17), keyed by permission exactly as NAV_GROUPS_RAW already does, and derive VALID_TABS, ActiveTab and the mobile TOC from it.

After the restructure: task A becomes 1 click (the requester name in the ticket header opens an inline account panel, see qols-03) with zero navigation. Task B becomes 0 clicks, the home view is the landing page, and a click only to drill into whatever is red. Task C stays 3 clicks; the win there is time-to-find, addressed separately in qols-06.

title: The admin landing view is ten headcount aggregates, none of which can go red, so there is no screen anywhere that answers whether anything is wrong right now
description:
The panel opens on the users tab (app/admin/page.tsx:203) and the only thing above the user table is two StatBar rows of five counters each (:1108-1179): Total Users, Total Scans, Scans 24h, 2FA Enabled, Disabled, New Users 7d, Active API Keys, Active Webhooks, Schedules, Shared Scans. Every one is a plain COUNT from the stats query at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:329-338. Not one can indicate a fault, and the code comment at app/admin/page.tsx:1103-1107 concedes they are not even clickable because the admin API takes only page, limit and search.

The signals that could go red exist but are each one nav click away and none is summarised anywhere. Scanner backlog: components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:72 computes `backedUp` and renders a destructive badge at :108-116, but only while that tab is mounted. Backup freshness: backup-manager.tsx:199-201 prints the newest file's mtime as plain text with no expected-interval comparison, so a backup that stopped running three weeks ago looks identical to one that ran this morning apart from a date the operator has to reason about. Security alerts, error logs, email delivery failures and support tickets are the same shape. Of the 20 nav items rendered at :1059-1094 exactly one carries a status indicator: the updater dot at :1087-1092.

This matters because AUDIT-012 found two failures that are silent by construction: #obs-02, a scheduled database backup that fails on every run still reports success to the failure escalator and writes no log line; #obs-03, worker failure escalation only sees pass-level throws, so a worker where every item failed resets its streak to zero and never alerts. Both are precisely the class of fault a health view exists to catch, and neither has any surface in the panel today.
impact: Nobody finds out the service is degraded from the admin panel. Backups can be dead for weeks (obs-02) and the Backups tab will show a stale date that reads as normal. A worker where every item errors (obs-03) shows no signal at all. The scanner queue can be backed up and the operator only learns when a user complains. On a service with about 50 real users and no on-call rotation, the admin panel is the whole monitoring story, and its front page is a vanity dashboard.
recommendation:
Add app/admin/(operations)/page.tsx as the panel's default landing view and change the initial activeTab at app/admin/page.tsx:203 to it. Render one status list, not a card grid: rows of `label / value / state`, each row green, amber or red, ordered worst-first, following the divided-list idiom in design-language.md D4 rather than adding a ninth stat strip. Rows to include, all buildable from endpoints that already exist:

- Scanner queue: reuse computeBackedUp and the stale-age thresholds already in components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts (STALE_PENDING_MS, STALE_RUNNING_MS). Red when backed up, amber when the oldest pending scan exceeds the stale threshold.
- Failed scans in the last 24 h: `counts.failedLast24h` from GET /api/v3/admin/queue-status. Amber above zero, red above a configurable share of completed.
- Backup age: from GET /api/v3/admin/backup's lastBackupAt, compared against the configured schedule interval rather than printed raw. Red when older than two intervals. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-02.
- Worker last success: add a per-worker last-success timestamp read and show age. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-03.
- Unresolved security alerts, error-log volume in the last hour, bounced or failed emails in the last 24 h, open support tickets, outstanding staff invites, update available.

Each row links to the tab that owns it. Mirror the worst state onto the nav item as a coloured dot, reusing the exact markup already at app/admin/page.tsx:1087-1092 so the operator sees a fault from any tab. Keep the ten headcount counters, but demote them to a collapsed Growth strip below the status list or move them to Billing Overview; they answer a business question, not an operational one.

title: db:restore pipes the dump into psql without ON_ERROR_STOP, so a restore in which every statement failed still prints "Restore complete." and exits 0
description: runRestore spawns `psql [connArg]` with no `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, no `--single-transaction`, and no `-q`. psql defaults ON_ERROR_STOP to off, so it prints each statement's error to stderr, continues with the next statement, and exits 0 as long as it consumed its input. The only failure check is `if (exitCode !== 0) throw` at line 108, which therefore never fires for SQL errors. backup-db.mjs produces the dump with `pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges --format=plain` (line 219), which contains no DROP statements and no CREATE DATABASE, so restoring into the DATABASE_URL the app has already booted against means every CREATE TABLE fails with "relation already exists" and every COPY into a table with existing rows fails on the primary key. All of those are non-fatal to psql. The script then reaches line 112 and prints "Restore complete." This is a different script and a different mechanism from AUDIT-012#obs-02 (which covers the scheduled backup job reporting success on failure); the backup artifact itself is correct here, plain-format pg_dump does capture schema, data and sequence setvals.
impact: The one command the project offers for disaster recovery cannot distinguish a complete restore from a total failure. The header comment tells operators to rehearse a restore against staging "before trusting it in a real incident", but the rehearsal will report success regardless of whether anything was actually restored, so the rehearsal proves nothing. In a real incident an operator will believe the database is recovered when it may contain none of the backed-up rows.
recommendation: In scripts/restore-db.mjs, spawn psql with `["-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "--single-transaction", connArg]` so the first error aborts with a non-zero exit and the whole restore rolls back rather than half-applying. Add a `--into-empty` preflight that counts public tables in the target and refuses to run when the target is non-empty unless an explicit `--force` is passed, and after a successful restore print the row counts of a few core tables so the operator has positive evidence.

title: The browser extension's 194-package dependency tree has no security monitoring at all: Dependabot only watches `/`, and the extension CI job never runs npm audit
category: no dependency monitoring on a shipped artifact
description: `.github/dependabot.yml` declares exactly two update configs, both scoped to the repo root: `package-ecosystem: "npm"` with `directory: "/"` (line 5) and `package-ecosystem: "github-actions"` with `directory: "/"` (line 84). Dependabot directories are not recursive, so `extension/package.json` and `extension/package-lock.json` (194 lockfile entries, of which 191 are dev) are never scanned and never produce a PR. The CI side has the same hole: the only audit step in the repo is `.github/workflows/ci.yml:71`, `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`, which runs in the `typecheck` job with the default working directory (repo root) and with `--omit=dev`. The separate `extension` job at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:115` runs `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, and `npm run build:chrome && npm run build:firefox` (lines 136 to 150) and has no audit step. The SBOM is generated by `anchore/sbom-action` against the built Docker image (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:82`), which contains the Next.js app and not the extension, so the extension zips attached to the release at `.github/workflows/release.yml:147` ship with no SBOM either. `--omit=dev` matters here specifically: the extension has only 2 runtime dependencies and 191 dev packages, and those dev packages (vite, rollup, esbuild, sharp, archiver) are the entire toolchain that produces `content.js`, the IIFE injected into every page the user visits via `content_scripts.matches: ["<all_urls>"]` (`extension/manifest/chrome.json:47`). A compromised build dependency writes straight into a browser-privileged artifact distributed through the Chrome Web Store and AMO. `npm audit --json` in `extension/` reports 0 vulnerabilities today, so nothing is currently exploitable; the finding is that nothing in the repo would tell anyone when that changes.
impact: A published CVE in any of the extension's 194 packages, including the build chain that emits the all-URLs content script, produces no Dependabot PR and no CI failure. The maintainer finds out only by manually running npm audit inside extension/, which nothing prompts them to do. For an extension already installed in users' browsers, the window between disclosure and a store update is unbounded.
recommendation: Add a third Dependabot config block with `package-ecosystem: "npm"` and `directory: "/extension"` (same schedule and labels as the root block), and add an `- name: Audit extension dependencies` / `run: npm audit --audit-level=high` step with `working-directory: extension` to the `extension` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` after the `npm ci` step at line 138. Do not pass `--omit=dev` there: for the extension the dev tree is the shipped tree.

title: The SSRF guard and the access-rule blocklist are stubbed permanently permissive in all three scan-route suites, so deleting both gates from the routes leaves the whole suite green
category: test would pass with the feature removed
description: Three route suites replace the two scan-target security gates with hard-coded always-allow stubs declared inline inside the vi.mock factory, so no test can override them and no test asserts they were even called. tests/app/api/v3/scan/route.test.ts:72 declares `validateScanTarget: vi.fn(async () => ({ safe: true }))` and :76 declares `checkAccessRules: vi.fn(async () => ({ allowed: true }))`. tests/app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.test.ts:68 and :75 do the same. tests/app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.test.ts:57 does it for checkAccessRules. A scripted scan of all 4,494 it/test blocks found zero occurrences of `safe: false` or a checkAccessRules `allowed: false` override in any of those three files, and zero `expect(validateScanTarget).toHaveBeenCalled` style assertions. The gates they stand in for are real: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:276 calls validateScanTarget and returns 400 on !safe, :285 calls checkAccessRules and returns 403 on !allowed; app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:304 and :310 do the same; app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:341 does the checkAccessRules half. The exact mutation the suite does not catch: delete lines 275 to 295 of app/api/v3/scan/route.ts, lines 304 to 313 of app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts, and lines 340 to 352 of app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts, and every one of the 697 lines of scan/route.test.ts plus both sibling suites still pass. For contrast, tests/app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.test.ts:179 does drive `mockCheckAccessRules.mockResolvedValue({ allowed: false })`, which is the pattern the three scan routes are missing.
impact: The SSRF gate on the main scan endpoint is the control that stops a user pointing a scan at 169.254.169.254 or an internal 10.x host, and the access-rule gate is the operator blocklist for restricted infrastructure. Both have been fixed by prior audits (AUDIT-011 demo-scan SSRF, AUDIT-012 rebinding work). Right now a refactor that drops either call from any of the three routes, or that moves the call after the scan is already dispatched, ships with a fully green CI run. The failure is silent until someone scans a metadata endpoint through the product.
recommendation: In each of the three suites, replace the inline `vi.fn(async () => ({ safe: true }))` factories with module-scope handles (`const mockValidateScanTarget = vi.fn(); vi.mock("@/lib/scanner/safe-fetch", () => ({ validateScanTarget: (...a) => mockValidateScanTarget(...a) }))`) defaulted to safe in beforeEach, then add two tests per route: one driving `{ safe: false, reason: "..." }` and asserting 400 plus that the scan was never dispatched (`expect(mockExecuteScan).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`), and one driving `{ allowed: false }` and asserting 403 with statusCode BLOCKED. Also assert `expect(mockValidateScanTarget).toHaveBeenCalledWith(normalizedUrl)` on the happy path so the call itself cannot be deleted.

title: The root layout awaits headers() for a CSP nonce, so all 311 routes render per-request and every one of the ~790 public pages is served private, no-cache, no-store
description: app/layout.tsx:146 does `const nonce = (await headers()).get("x-nonce")` to feed the nonce on the inline auth-cache <script> at app/layout.tsx:158. Reading headers() in the root layout opts every segment beneath it into per-request dynamic rendering. The committed build proves it: .next/prerender-manifest.json lists exactly 5 prerendered routes (/robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /manifest.webmanifest, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt) and 0 dynamicRoutes, against 311 entries in .next/app-build-manifest.json. app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:34 still runs generateStaticParams() over all ~754 checks at build time and produces nothing; its own comment at line 29 acknowledges this ('The root layout reads headers() for its CSP nonce, so the whole app already renders per-request'). Next.js sets `cache-control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` on dynamically-rendered app pages (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/cache-control.js:15), and nothing in middleware.ts or next.config.mjs overrides it -- grepping Cache-Control across middleware.ts and lib/ returns one unrelated hit in lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:142. So /checks/*, /checks/category/*, /alternatives/*, /docs/*, /changelog, /pricing, /compare and /landing are all re-rendered from scratch on every single request and are uncacheable by the browser, by Cloudflare, and by any CDN in front of the app.
impact: The entire SEO surface, which is the product's growth engine (~754 /checks pages plus category, docs, alternatives and compare pages), pays a full origin React render on every crawler hit and every visitor, with zero edge caching. A search-engine crawl of the check index is ~790 cold SSRs against one Node process that is also running scans. TTFB for anonymous marketing traffic is pinned to origin latency rather than the CDN, and traffic spikes hit the origin directly instead of being absorbed by Cloudflare.
recommendation: Drop the nonce. The inline script at app/layout.tsx:158 is build-time constant (its only interpolation is JSON.stringify over STAFF_ROLES), so compute its sha256 at build and put 'sha256-...' in the script-src of middleware.ts instead of 'nonce-...'; then delete the `await headers()` at app/layout.tsx:146 and the nonce prop. With the layout static, add `export const revalidate` to app/checks/[id]/page.tsx, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx and the docs pages so generateStaticParams actually produces ISR-cached HTML. If the nonce must stay, move the nonce-consuming script into a route-group layout that only wraps the authenticated app (/dashboard, /history, /profile, /admin, ...) and leave the public marketing/SEO group on a static layout.

title: GET /api/v3/badge/[token] joins scan_history on url with no usable index, so the most hotlinked public endpoint in the product does a sequential scan of the whole scans table per request
category: missing index on a public hot path
description: The badge route runs `FROM host_badges hb JOIN scan_history sh ON sh.url = hb.url AND (sh.user_id = hb.user_id OR (hb.scope = 'global' AND sh.is_public = true)) WHERE hb.badge_token_hash = $1 AND hb.revoked_at IS NULL AND sh.status = 'completed' ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC LIMIT 1` (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:66-74). The only index touching `scan_history.url` is `idx_scan_history_url_public_completed ON scan_history(url) WHERE is_public = true AND status = 'completed'` (instrumentation.ts:2359-2361). Because the `sh.user_id = hb.user_id` half of the OR is deliberately NOT gated on `is_public` (see the comment at app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:51-52), the query's predicate does not imply the index's partial predicate and Postgres cannot use it. There is no unconditional index on `scan_history(url)`. The identical join shape appears at app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:59-67 and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/screenshot/route.ts:50-57.
impact: A status badge is an embedded in third-party READMEs and websites; it is by construction the highest-request-rate route in the app and it is unauthenticated. Every hit currently seq-scans scan_history. At 10k scan rows that is already tens of milliseconds of pure I/O per badge render; it degrades linearly forever and there is no cache in front of it.
recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_scan_history_url_scanned ON scan_history(url, scanned_at DESC);` to the performance-index block in instrumentation.ts (near line 1587). The same index also serves the `DISTINCT ON (url) ... ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` sorts in app/api/v3/badge/scans/route.ts:24-31 and lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:81-91, and the `WHERE user_id = $1 AND url = $2 ORDER BY scanned_at DESC LIMIT 1` lookup in lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts:63-65 that runs after every completed scan.

title: The admin broadcast send loads every verified user with no LIMIT, then does two queries plus one SMTP round trip per recipient, sequentially
description: `const usersResult = await pool.query(userQuery, queryParams)` at app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:552 executes a query built from `SELECT u.id, u.email FROM users u WHERE u.email_verified_at IS NOT NULL` plus optional plan/preference filters -- no LIMIT, no batching, the whole verified user base materialized into Node memory. The loop at line 553 then runs, per recipient and strictly in order: a `SELECT 1 FROM broadcast_recipients WHERE message_id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status = 'sent' LIMIT 1` (line 558), an `await sendEmail(...)` (line 563), and an `INSERT INTO broadcast_recipients` (line 571). `broadcast_recipients` has only the separate single-column indexes `idx_broadcast_recipients_message` and `idx_broadcast_recipients_user` (instrumentation.ts:1160-1161), no `(message_id, user_id)` composite, so the dedupe check at 558 rescans one of those lists per iteration. The identical code is duplicated for the `resend` action at lines 714-743.
impact: Sending one broadcast to N users costs 1 + 2N database round trips and N sequential SMTP handshakes on a single pooled connection, inside one HTTP request. At today's ~50 users that is ~100 queries and a minute of blocking; the shape does not scale, and the request will time out long before the send finishes at any real size, leaving the broadcast half-delivered.
recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_broadcast_recipients_msg_user ON broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id);` and replace the per-row dedupe SELECT with a real UNIQUE constraint plus `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Page the recipient query with `LIMIT`/keyset pagination and move the send itself to the background worker pattern already used by lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.ts (`runInBatches`, line 393), which caps concurrency explicitly.

title: Five real OAuth error codes render an empty string, so a failed Discord sign-in shows a normal login form
description: The ?error= mapper at app/login/page.tsx:47-89 has no catch-all and ends in `return ""`. Five codes the OAuth callback actually emits are unmapped: discord_invalid, discord_not_configured, discord_invalid_state, discord_user_failed, session_expired.
impact: A Discord sign-in that fails for any of these reasons bounces the user back to a login form that looks completely normal, with no message at all. They retry and fail identically, with no path to understanding why.
recommendation: Add a catch-all before `return ""`, for example 'Sign-in failed. Try again, or use another method.'

title: The findings bulk-remediation toolbar is the only true bulk action in the product, and it is poor enough to justify removal
description: Select mode lives at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:122-226 with the toggle at :440-458, the row checkbox at :659-669 and the bulk bar at :685-770. It is gated by scanUrl from canRemediate (components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:71-74) so it appears only on /dashboard after a scan and on /history?id=n. Four specific problems: (1) in select mode the row body is still a full-width button that navigates (:811-813), and opening a finding unmounts ResultsList entirely (its own comment at :228-234 says so) while selected, selectMode and overlay are all local useState, so one mis-tap on row 38 of 200 wipes the selection with no persistence anywhere; (2) selection ignores filters silently, so narrowing the severity filter leaves hidden picks selected and Apply hits findings the user cannot see; (3) at 360px the bar wraps to three rows, roughly 130-160px, a quarter of the viewport, pinned over the list being selected from, one of those rows being a cramped native date picker; (4) the backend is a bulk endpoint in name only, fanning out to Promise.all of up to 200 independent pool.query calls with no transaction (app/api/v3/scan/remediation/bulk/route.ts:83-119), so partial failure leaves partial state behind a generic 'Couldn't apply. Try again.' There is no select-all, no per-group select, no shift-click range, no keyboard toggle (shiftKey appears nowhere in the repo), no confirmation and no undo, and status 'open' deletes each row including notes and assignees irreversibly.
impact: The one place multi-select carries real weight, triaging the 100+ findings a crawl scan produces, is the place it works worst. Users lose selections to mis-taps and cannot tell which findings an Apply actually touched.
recommendation: Owner's call, and both paths are costed. REMOVE is roughly 565 lines: results-list.tsx ~235 (893 to ~660), the route 128, its tests 111, openapi-spec.ts ~35, docs/triage ~40, docs-knowledge.md ~15, plus one line each in client-constants.ts:226, scan-result-detail.tsx, dashboard-results.tsx:232 and history/page.tsx:499. useTeammates survives (issue-detail.tsx:296 also uses it) and the per-finding RemediationControl remains as the fallback. REDESIGN is roughly two days: delete the mode toggle and make the row's left severity bar a 36px selection target; lift selection into lib/hooks/use-finding-selection.ts backed by sessionStorage keyed on scanUrl so it survives navigation; add tri-state select-all on the count line and on each severity group header; collapse the toolbar to '[N selected] [Mark as v] [Clear]' on desktop and a full-width action sheet of five 44px rows on mobile; add x to toggle, shift-click to extend, Esc to clear; replace confirmation with an 8-second Undo, which requires capturing prior remediation rows and giving the route an items[] body shape; and replace the Promise.all fan-out with one INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM unnest(...) inside a transaction so the all-or-nothing error copy becomes honest.

title: The monthly to yearly upgrade has no entry point because the current-plan check ignores billing interval
description: components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:124 is `const isCurrentPlan = currentPlan === plan.id;`, which ignores the billing interval. Flipping the hero's -20% monthly/yearly toggle still renders a disabled 'Current Plan' button for a user on the monthly tier.
impact: /checkout/pro_supporter_yearly is reachable only by typing the URL, even though app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:199 already ships 'Switch to yearly billing' copy for it. The 20 percent annual upsell has no entry point anywhere in the product.
recommendation: Compare the billing interval as well as the plan id.

title: 'Go to the dashboard now' does not navigate, stranding the user on a success screen during a slow confirmation
description: components/billing/stripe-checkout.tsx:121 calls onSuccess(), which renders the 'You are subscribed' screen while confirmation is still retrying, and never navigates anywhere. The three credit components use a real <Link>.
impact: The user clicks the escape hatch during a slow confirmation and is left on a success screen for a subscription that may not have confirmed.
recommendation: Use <Link href={ROUTES.DASHBOARD}> as the three sibling components do.

title: /compare fails silently and permanently on every error, with an explicitly no-op catch
description: app/compare/page.tsx:54-64 fetches the compare endpoint, sets diffResult only `if (res.ok)`, has no else branch, and catches with `/* ignore */`. A 403 (a shared link to someone else's scans), a 404 (deleted scan), a 500 or a dropped connection all land identically: loading flips false, diffResult stays null, and the UI re-renders the scan picker with the Compare button live again. app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:238-240 already has the correct pattern in-repo.
impact: The user clicks Compare, watches a spinner, and is returned exactly where they started with no explanation. Clicking again reproduces it forever. A shared /compare link the recipient cannot access shows the generic host picker with no hint why.
recommendation: Add an error state set in both the non-ok branch and the catch, rendered above the Compare button.

title: POST /api/v3/scan/bulk is fully built and has no UI caller; the dashboard loops single scans instead
description: app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts is 734 lines and accepts {urls[], isPublic}, scanning up to a plan-capped 100 URLs in one request. API.SCAN_BULK is declared at lib/config/constants.ts:747 and referenced by nothing outside the docs pages and landing-api-example.tsx:118. The dashboard's bulk panel instead loops POST /api/v3/scan one URL at a time at app/dashboard/page.tsx:743-775, and detects rate limits by string-matching error text at :762-763. The two paths have separately-audited quota and privacy handling. Note also that FEATURE_BULK_SCANS gates only the unused public endpoint (scan/bulk/route.ts:346), so disabling the flag does not disable the dashboard's bulk tab.
impact: The first-party UI pays N round trips for what the server does in one, repeatedly trips its own burst limiter, reports failure per URL instead of atomically, and diverges from the audited code path. Bulk scanning is a sold plan feature priced 5/10/25/100 across tiers.
recommendation: Point handleBulkScan at API.SCAN_BULK with the whole array. Roughly 40 lines out of app/dashboard/page.tsx replaced by about 15, and the feature flag starts working.

title: Plan limits displayed to users come from a hardcoded catalog while enforcement reads 48 admin-editable settings
description: components/pricing/pricing-features.tsx:186-187 carries the comment 'These numbers come straight out of the billing config, so this table cannot drift from what the API actually enforces', but it reads PLANS[].limits from lib/billing/catalog.ts:115-233, a hardcoded copy. Enforcement reads the 48 BILLING_* registry settings via lib/billing/plan-limits.ts:19-82. The same hardcoded read occurs at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:157, components/modals/premium-upgrade-modal.tsx:79/89, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:204,223,294, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1493 and app/pricing/page.tsx:28-36. It is done correctly at app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 and app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:111,184, which resolve live.
impact: Values match today so there is no present drift, but any one of 48 admin edits silently desynchronises what is advertised from what is enforced, on the pricing page, in the upgrade modal and on the checkout page. The comment asserting this cannot happen makes it less likely anyone checks.
recommendation: Have the display surfaces resolve limits live the way app/api/v3/billing/route.ts:82-94 does, and delete the comment at pricing-features.tsx:186-187.

title: The scanning page timer undersells the engine and should be removed once the latency is fixed
description: components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 starts a pure client stopwatch with useState(() => Date.now()), ticked at :149 and rendered at :271-273. It starts at setStatus('scanning') in app/dashboard/page.tsx:471, before the POST at :537, and stops only when React unmounts the indicator at :910. It floors the value (:77-81), so a displayed '17s' means at least 17.0 real seconds. Separately, the server-reported 'Scan duration' stat (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:303-310, from result.duration, snapshotted at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:823) also includes the subdomain wait since commit 3a242f89. Both numbers are honest and both show roughly 17s. The 2-5s engine time is not surfaced anywhere in the product. Verified NOT the cause: there is no artificial minimum display time (the cosmetic timers at :42, :58, :69 cannot hold the flip because the component is unmounted by the status conditional), no serial post-completion fetches, and no router.refresh().
impact: The product's core differentiator is speed, and the only number the user watches contradicts it on every scan.
recommendation: Fix scan-01 first. Then replace the elapsed-seconds readout with progress that carries information rather than a number that invites comparison: the check family currently running, the count of checks completed against the total, and the findings counter ticking up as they land. If a duration is shown at all after the fix, show the server-reported engine time and label it as such.

title: The AI chat launcher covers the Save Changes button on /profile and the bottom-right of every commerce form
description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1613-1617 renders a 56px FAB at bottom-5 right-5 z-50, mounted after children. Its route gating at :1273-1284 returns null on /browser/, /docs and /admin, but not /profile. At 375px the save card spans to right:16px with right-aligned buttons, so the FAB occupying right 20-76px and y 20-76px sits directly over Save Changes.
impact: Compounds shell-02 on /profile: even after dismissing the cookie notice, the chat launcher still covers the save button on a phone. Also covers the bottom-right of forms on /pricing, /checkout, /contact, /legal and the auth pages.
recommendation: Offset the launcher by --vr-cookie-h and give the floating save bars right padding that clears 76px on mobile, or add /profile to the launcher's null-return route list.

title: The teammate scan 'View' button links to a hash the history page never reads, using the wrong id
description: components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:107 renders `<a href={`/history#${scan.id}`}>`. /history reads only ?scan=<public_id> (app/history/page.tsx:161,176-178) and nothing anywhere reads location.hash. Compounding this, MemberScan.id is the numeric primary key (components/teams/teams-types.ts:47), not the opaque public_id the route resolves.
impact: Clicking View drops the user on the unfiltered history list with no indication of what happened. Both halves are wrong, so even adding hash handling would not fix it.
recommendation: Return public_id from /api/v3/teams/member-scans and link to `/history?scan=${scan.publicId}`.

title: Teammate scan panel can display one member's scans under another member's name
description: app/teams/page.tsx:459-481 sets viewingMember unconditionally at :464 and only assigns memberScans inside the `if (res.ok)` branch at :472. memberScans is never cleared. After a successful load for member A, a failed load for member B leaves A's scan list in state while the heading renders `{member.name}'s Scan History` (components/teams/team-member-scans.tsx:45). The memberScansReqRef ticket guards response ordering but not the error path, which is the same class of mislabel it was written to prevent.
impact: One teammate's scanned URLs are displayed under a different teammate's name. On a team feature this is a trust and privacy problem, not just a rendering bug.
recommendation: Call setMemberScans([]) before the fetch and add an explicit error branch that renders a failure state rather than leaving stale data on screen.

title: A scan in flight during any process restart is left stuck at 'running' forever, with no automatic recovery
description: Scan cancellation and the scan watchdog are purely in-memory and per-process (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts's own header comment concedes this explicitly: 'a scan whose process dies mid-run is left at running with no in-process timer left to rescue it'). The watchdog is a plain setTimeout closure tied to execute-scan.ts's call stack, so it is lost on any restart, not just a crash -- including a routine `docker compose restart`/redeploy. instrumentation.ts's graceful-shutdown handler (SIGTERM/SIGINT) only closes the DB connection pool; it never marks in-flight scan_history rows as failed/interrupted. lib/database/cleanup.ts, which runs a periodic sweep for every other kind of stale row in this app, has no logic that resets stale 'running'/'pending' scan_history rows on startup. The only way to clear a stuck row is the manual DELETE /api/v3/scan/status/[id] cancel endpoint, which nothing calls automatically and which the History UI does not surface for a scan that wasn't started in the current browser session. Net effect: every deploy that lands while any scan is mid-flight leaves that scan permanently spinning in the user's dashboard/history with no error message and no self-heal. Evidence: lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts lines 12-16 (doc comment) and lines 121-129 (startWatchdog, in-memory setTimeout); instrumentation.ts lines 2965-2975 (gracefulShutdown only calls pool.end()); grep for "status IN ('pending', 'running')" / "status = 'running'" across lib and app shows only lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts touches these states -- no reaper anywhere else; app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts DELETE handler is the only path that can clear a stuck row, and it requires the user to know to call it.
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: On boot (instrumentation.ts), sweep scan_history for rows still 'pending'/'running' with started_at older than the max scan timeout and flip them to 'failed' with a reason like 'Interrupted by server restart.' Optionally also attempt this in the SIGTERM handler before pool.end() so a graceful restart doesn't even create the window.
